DRAFT -- Partnership Language for USAID - Facebook
USAID and Facebook seek to pursue a more formalized strategic partnership to advance our mutual
interests in developing countries around the world.
This partnership will be built on our shared values that respect the voice, dignity, rights and safety of the
communities and individuals that we serve.
The goal of this partnership will be to target USAID investments to its local partners and provide USAID
local partners with streamlined access to Facebook tools, training and trusted partner networks that
address information integrity and content that has potential to cause harm. The partnership would
potentially include:
• USAID identification and support of partners for access to research technologies: Process
and point of contact by which USAID partners can get access to Facebook's CrowdTangle
platform to inform the design of USAID-funded projects and understand public engagement of
content posted on Facebook and Instagram.
• USAID identification and support of partners for access to ad credits: Process and point of
contact by which USAID partners can apply for ad credits and toolkits to be more effective on
Facebook products to raise awareness and address shared problems (e.g. hate speech, violent
extremism, dis/misinformation, Covid-19, promotion of authoritative information etc.).
• USAID identification and support of partners for participation in partnership programs:
Process and point of contact by which USAID can refer local partners interested in participating
in Facebook's networks and programs including:
• International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN): to participate in third-party fact-checking
and verification programs and receive IFCN certification.
• Trusted Partners: to provide market knowledge, conduct harm assessments and identify
context-appropriate risk mitigation approaches.
• Info-Centers: participation in the generation of content to be highlighted on Facebook's
Info Centers (i.e Climate Science Info Center, Voting Info Center, Covid Info Center).
• Digital Literacy Initiatives.
• Identification of touch points at USAID and at Facebook for collaboration and coordination
on countries of concern:
• Sharing an annually updated list of countries of concern.
• Process and point of contact by which State/USAID and its partners can raise concerns
and get feedback related to the violation of Facebook's community values, policies, and
terms of service, including inauthentic behavior on the platform.

Point of contact on Facebook's Product Support Team to coordinate technical training for
USAID partners and answer questions on platform features, including authorization to
publish ads funded by USAID.
Point of contact on Facebook's Election Team to coordinate support related to voter
education, election observation and flag potential spoilers or destabilizers to the political
transition.

• Point of contact for Facebook's Information Hubs to refer local partners who are pushing
authoritative content on trending whole-of-society issues (e.g. Covid-19, climate change,
etc.) and looking to maximize their reach.
Acceptance of common language to build in information-domain interventions into
agreements.
